newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee slips on NY, stops triggered.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee slips on NY, stops triggered.

text.p: LIFFE coffee futures took a tumble in switch-dominated trade on Monday morning after a sharply lower close in New York on Monday.
The market gapped just $3-$5 down at the open against pre-market opening expectations of $50-$60 lower.
The decline accelerated after benchmark November triggered stop-loss selling at $1,475, pushing the contract to a session low of $1,445.
It then regained some ground but still ended the midsession $30 lower at $1,474.
But traders doubt if the extra selling below $1,475 came on the back of the slightly bearish U.S. green coffee stocks data, released after the close of the New York trading on Friday.
The stock report showed a 219,000 60-kg bags fall in July against earlier expectations of 50,000 to 150,000 bags.
Based on London's performance, traders called the New York arabica market to open unchanged.
Overall volume stood at 2,735 lots, with two-thirds were in switches. Sept/Nov was traded at $15-$20 and Sept/Jan at level money.
Technically, traders said the market could bounce back if the $1,475 support holds.
If it fails, the market could slip further towards the next major support at the $1,390-$1,424 chart gap.
Broker GNI said the U.S. stock news could create a sell off in New York at the start of this week, particularly as the U.S. technicals were now following the London lead and turning negative.
"However London has been predominantly sold off on the back of the slump in the Indonesian rupiah as the currency has floated," it said in a commentary on Monday.

In other news, Vietnam's next coffee crop is expected to be a bumper one with yields of robusta and arabica reaching as much as 350,000 tonnes, according to the head of the Vietnam Coffee Corporation (Vinacafe).
Tran Khai was quoted by the English-language Vietnam News on Saturday as saying the 1997/98 crop would be Vietnam's biggest so far. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
